corrected_value.title: The effects of torture: Two community studies
corrected_value.authors: Kira, I., Templin, T., Lewandowski, L., Clifford, D., Wiencek, E., Hammad, A., Al-Haidar, A., & Mohanesh, J.

decisions.quote: Partial correlation and hierarchical regression results found that torture trauma and torture severity were not significant predictors of PTSD, other cumulative life traumas that happened before and after torture were the highly significant predictors. These results replicated previous findings of Kira et al., 2006;and Hollifield et al., 2011.
decisions.reason: Omitted target: the paper introduces Kira et al. (2006) in the Introduction as finding that torture did not predict PTSD after controlling for cumulative traumas before and after torture, directly re-tests this relationship in Hypothesis 1 using the CTS in a new clinical sample of 326 torture survivors, and explicitly states in the Discussion that the results replicated the findings of both Kira et al. (2006) and Hollifield et al. (2011) (outcome: successful).

corrected_value.title: A multivariate contextual analysis of torture and cruel, inhuman, and degrading treatments: Implications for an evidence-based definition of torture

decisions.quote: For torture types, while physical torture did not predict PTSD or CTD, witnessing or psychological torture predicted CTD, and PTSD, replicating Basoglu et al.'s (2009) findings.
decisions.reason: Omitted target: the paper reviews Başoglu (2009) in the Introduction as finding that psychological torture rather than physical torture predicts PTSD, tests the differential effects of physical vs. witnessing/psychological torture subscales in a new clinical sample, and explicitly reports in the Discussion that these results replicated Başoglu et al.'s (2009) findings (outcome: successful).

corrected_value.title: Classifying the torture experiences of refugees living in the United States
corrected_value.authors: Hooberman, J., Rosenfeld, B., Lhewa, D., Rasmussen, A., & Keller, A.

decisions.quote: Anal rape was associated with PTSD and CTD. Vaginal rape predicted CTD. These results replicated Hooberman et al., 2007, andPunamaki et al., 2010 findings on the development of PTSD symptom following sexual torture.
decisions.reason: Omitted target: the paper introduces Hooberman et al. (2007) in the Introduction as finding that torture rape was the factor associated with PTSD symptoms, tests sexual torture (anal and vaginal rape) as predictors of PTSD and CTD in Hypothesis 2 and hierarchical regressions in a new sample, and explicitly concludes in the Discussion that the results replicated Hooberman et al. (2007) (outcome: successful).

corrected_value.authors: Punamäki, R., Qouta, S. R., & EI Sarraj, E.

decisions.quote: Anal rape was associated with PTSD and CTD. Vaginal rape predicted CTD. These results replicated Hooberman et al., 2007, andPunamaki et al., 2010 findings on the development of PTSD symptom following sexual torture.
decisions.reason: Omitted target: the paper cites Punamäki et al. (2010) in the Introduction on torture components and mental health outcomes, re-tests specific torture components including sexual torture in a new clinical sample, and explicitly states in the Discussion that the results replicated Punamäki et al. (2010) findings on the development of PTSD symptoms following sexual torture (outcome: successful).
